limitations: M1 usage acceptance only. No M2 game, complete ray tracing, or extra feature tests. The 472-test suite and the mainline eleven gates were not rerun or claimed as independently verified here.
Only this Windows machine with headed Chromium and the recorded hardware WebGPU adapter was tested; no cross-device/performance claim.
The supplied wrapper prepared locked dependencies with npm ci --prefer-offline. setup --offline then reported dependencies and the user Playwright browser cache reused.
Snapshot/replay equality covers the engine-owned state in the preserved JSON snapshots, not arbitrary external IO or cross-GPU bit identity.

Browser automation uses the frozen tools/browser-session.ts helper and numeric polling=100 with Node deadlines. External test scripts import this tooling helper only; game code imports only the public SDK.
Development servers were intentionally force-closed by verified owned PID trees. Dev-start exitCode denotes successful launcher/readiness, not a natural long-running server exit.

A supplemental first unattended probe failed an opaque assertion with pre-created same-context cover tab; original failed JSON and command attempts are retained. Corrected probes follow documented isolated browser.newPage order and passed. This did not reset or bypass any CLI restore/replay session.

The unattended probes created an owned covering blank page without activating the game, but document.hasFocus reported true in both samples. No stronger OS foreground/occlusion guarantee is inferred; zero required clicks, keypresses and bringToFront calls is directly recorded.

incidents.resolution: Read available browser-session.ts and actual renderer public protocol instead; no runtime impact.
